subject: general
question: If (p - q) = - 6, (q - r) = 5 and (r - p) = 1, then find the value of (p³ + q³ + r³ - 3pqr)/(p + q + r).
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **algebraic identity** for the given expression is:

(p³ + q³ + r³ − 3pqr) / (p + q + r) = ½ × [(p − q)² + (q − r)² + (r − p)²]

Substitute the given differences: ½ × [(−6)² + 5² + 1²]

⇒ ½ × [36 + 25 + 1] = 62 / 2 = 31

**∴ The correct answer is 31.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(p − q) = −6

(q − r) = 5

(r − p) = 1

**Formula Used:**

p³ + q³ + r³ − 3pqr = (p + q + r) × ½ × [(p − q)² + (q − r)² + (r − p)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8381ea150e16e7a14dbd94113d6cc43829e1c05c58c4bed4f34432c3e0d316c2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Target = (p³ + q³ + r³ − 3pqr) / (p + q + r)

⇒ Target = [(p + q + r) × ½ × {(p − q)² + (q − r)² + (r − p)²}] / (p + q + r)

⇒ Target = ½ × [(−6)² + 5² + 1²]

⇒ Target = ½ × [36 + 25 + 1]

⇒ Target = 62 / 2

⇒ Target = 31

**∴ The correct answer is 31.**

**__Additional Information__**

The Cube Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). This is a fundamental expansion used in algebraic simplifications.

Sum of Squares Alternative

The expression (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) can always be written as ½[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²], which is useful when differences are known.

Special Case: a + b + c = 0

If the sum of the variables is zero, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc. This is frequently tested in competitive exams.

Special Case: a = b = c

If all three variables are equal, then the value of the expression a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc is always zero.</p
